summary:
[  edit  ]
The Math  CHOP  performs arithmetic operations on channels. The channels of a  CHOP  can be combined into one channel, and several CHOPs can be combined into one  CHOP .
The OP page lets you pre-operate on each sample, like making all samples positive or taking the square  of each sample.
Using  Combine Channels , for an input  CHOP  with multi-channels, you can multiply the samples of one channel by the samples in the other channels, reducing N channels down to one. You can combine them by multiplying, adding, finding the maximum, etc..
Using  Combine CHOPs , where there are two or more  CHOP  inputs, you can multiply (or add, etc.) the channels in one  CHOP  with the channels in all the other CHOPs, reducing N CHOPs to 1. (otherwise channels of multi-inputs are just merged)
You can then post-operate on the resulting samples - negate, square root, etc.
Then using the Mult-Add page it can offset and scale the values of each sample.
More conveniently you can use the Range page to do linear scaling as well by setting an output low-high range for a certain input low-high range.
Finally, you can round the resulting values off to an integer.
Tip : You can affect only certain channels of your input by using the  Scope  parameter on the Common page.
Note : To do logic operations (and, or, ...) between channels or CHOPs, use the  Logic CHOP .
Tip: Customizing each channel: : You can use the local member  chanIndex  in a parameter like Post-Add, for example,  me.chanIndex*2  to give a different post-add value for each channel.  chanIndex  is available in numerous CHOPs like the  Pattern CHOP . (expressions are non-optimized)

parameters.label: Channel Pre  OP
parameters.name: preop
parameters.description: ⊞  - Unary operations can be performed on individual channels. A menu of unary operations (as described above) that are performed on each channel as it comes in to the Math  CHOP  include:

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Don't do anything to the channel.

parameters.label: Negate
parameters.name: negate
parameters.description: Take the negative value of each sample of the channel.

parameters.label: Positive
parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: Make negative values of the channel positive (absolute).

parameters.label: Root
parameters.name: root
parameters.description: Take the square root of all values in the channel.

parameters.label: Square
parameters.name: square
parameters.description: Square all the values in the channel.

parameters.label: Inverse
parameters.name: inverse
parameters.description: Take the inverse (1/x) of all values in the channel.

parameters.label: Combine Channels
parameters.name: chanop
parameters.description: ⊞  - A choice of operations is performed between the channels of an input  CHOP , for each input. The Nth sample of one channel is combined with the Nth sample of other channels:

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Don't combine the channels.

parameters.label: Add
parameters.name: add
parameters.description: Sum all the channels.

parameters.label: Subtract
parameters.name: sub
parameters.description: Subtract all the channels from the first.

parameters.label: Multiply
parameters.name: mul
parameters.description: Multiply all the channels.

parameters.label: Divide
parameters.name: div
parameters.description: Divide the first channel by all the rest.

parameters.label: Average
parameters.name: avg
parameters.description: Take the average of all the channels.

parameters.label: Minimum
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Take the minimum value of all the channels.

parameters.label: Maximum
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Take the maximum value of all the channels.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.name: len
parameters.description: Assume the channels are a vector and compute its length.

parameters.label: Combine CHOPs
parameters.name: chopop
parameters.description: ⊞  - A menu of operations that is performed between the input CHOPs, combining several CHOPs into one.

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Don't combine the channels.

parameters.label: Add
parameters.name: add
parameters.description: Sum all the channels.

parameters.label: Subtract
parameters.name: sub
parameters.description: Subtract all the channels from the first.

parameters.label: Multiply
parameters.name: mul
parameters.description: Multiply of all the channels.

parameters.label: Divide
parameters.name: div
parameters.description: Divide the first channel by all the rest.

parameters.label: Average
parameters.name: avg
parameters.description: Take the average of all the channels.

parameters.label: Minimum
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Take the minimum value of all the channels.

parameters.label: Maximum

parameters.description: Take the maximum value of all the channels.

parameters.label: Length

parameters.description: Assume the channels are a vector and compute its length.

parameters.label: Channel Post  OP
parameters.name: postop
parameters.description: ⊞  - A menu (same as Channel Pre  OP ) is performed as the finale stage upon the channels resulting from the above operations.

parameters.label: Match by
parameters.name: match
parameters.description: ⊞  - Match channels between inputs by name or index.

parameters.label: Align
parameters.name: align
parameters.description: ⊞  - This menu handles cases where multiple input CHOPs have different start or end times. All channels output from a  CHOP  share the same start/end interval, so the inputs must be treated with the Align Options:

parameters.label: Automatic
parameters.name: auto
parameters.description: It will trim to the current  Time Slice  if there are any Time Slices, else it will do an Extend Min/Max.

parameters.label: Extend to Min/Max
parameters.name: none
parameters.description: Find the earliest start and latest end, and extend all inputs to that range using the extend conditions. (see  Extend Conditions ).

parameters.label: Stretch to Min/Max
parameters.name: stretch
parameters.description: Find the earliest start and latest end, and stretch every channel's start and end to that range.

parameters.label: Shift to Minimum
parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Find the earliest start and shift all channels so they all start at that index. All channels are extended to the length of the longest one.

parameters.label: Shift to Maximum
parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Find the latest end and shift all channels so they all end at that index. Extend all channels to the length of the longest one.

parameters.label: Shift to First Interval
parameters.name: shift1
parameters.description: Shift all channels to the start of the first  CHOP  and sample all inputs using the first input's range.

parameters.label: Trim to First Interval
parameters.name: trim1
parameters.description: Trim all channels to first  CHOP 's range.

parameters.label: Stretch to First Interval
parameters.name: stretch1
parameters.description: Stretch all channels to the first  CHOP 's range.

parameters.label: Trim to Smallest Interval
parameters.name: trim
parameters.description: Trim all channels to the smallest start/end interval. The start and end values may not come from the same channel.

parameters.label: Stretch to Smallest Interval
parameters.name: squash
parameters.description: Stretch all channels to the smallest start/end interval. The start and end values may not come from the same channel.

parameters.label: Interp Pars per  Sample
parameters.name: interppars
parameters.description: Use this option when the input is a higher frequency than the timeline (example: audio).  It will avoid any pops or crackles in the output when adjusting the multiply, add or  range parameters.

parameters.label: Integer
parameters.name: integer
parameters.description: ⊞  - The resulting values can be converted to integer.

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Don't affect the value.

parameters.label: Ceiling
parameters.name: ceiling
parameters.description: Round a value up to the next integer.

parameters.label: Floor
parameters.name: floor
parameters.description: Round a value down to the next integer.

parameters.label: Round
parameters.name: round
parameters.description: Round a value to the nearest integer.

parameters.label: Pre-Add
parameters.name: preoff
parameters.description: First, add the value to each sample of each channel.

parameters.label: Multiply
parameters.name: gain
parameters.description: Then multiply by this value.

parameters.label: Post-Add
parameters.name: postoff
parameters.description: Then add this value.

parameters.label: From Range
parameters.name: fromrange
parameters.description: ⊞  - Another way to multiply/add. Converts from one low-high range to another range.

parameters.label: To Range
parameters.name: torange
parameters.description: ⊞  - Another way to multiply/add. Converts from one low-high range to another range.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
